tender.description:
The Contract will principally comprise landscape maintenance and common close cleaning services.
The landscape maintenance services will mainly include litter picking, grass cutting, shrub bed, hedging and leaf collection to existing properties and common landscaped areas throughout Cardonald and Pollokshields, Glasgow to the areas detailed within the Landscape Architects tender drawings.  The Contract may also include tree maintenance services, tree and stump removal works, and repairs to existing damaged grass and other landscaped areas.
The landscape maintenance will initially be undertaken to estates located at St Andrews Drive, Queensland Community Garden and Halfway Community Park, however Southside Housing Association may introduce additional estates during the Contract that are located on the south side of Glasgow which shall be valued at the rates within Tender Document A where the maintenance requirements are similar in character.  This contract is anticipated to include two estates where Southside Housing Association do not have landscape architects Maps or quantities at the date of inviting tenders.
The Common Close Cleaning maintenance requirements will principally involve weekly internal and external cleaning to properties, and also monthly, quarterly & six monthly cleaning activities (refer Specification Items 1-21 described within Tender Document C ‘Common Close Cleaning Specification’ for further information).
Bidders are also advised that Southside Housing Association may extend the common close cleaning requirement of the Contract to additional locations throughout the south side of Glasgow to take account of any changes to requirements or new stock acquired during the Contract.
Bidders are also advised that Glasgow City Council are currently introducing an on-street bin replacement programme.   If any of the common close cleaning properties listed in the tender documentation participate in Glasgow City Council’s on-street replacement programme in the future, cleaning of the existing bin store areas to the property may no longer be required during the Contract.
In the event that cleaning of the bin store areas to a property is no longer required during the Contract, Southside Housing Association may instruct omission of the bin store cleaning to the property from the Contract and deduct the Contractor’s cost for the bin store cleaning to the property without loss or recompense to the Contractor.
Southside Housing Association may also omit any of the landscape maintenance estates or common close cleaning properties listed within the tender documentation at any time during the Contract where a landscape maintenance estate or common close cleaning property is no longer in ownership, factored by Southside Housing Association or Southside Housing Association are unable to obtain authorisation to proceed with the services to a property where consent from factored owners has not been obtained.
No loss or recompense will be due to the Contractor if Southside Housing Association omit any of the landscape maintenance estates or common close cleaning properties during the Contract where estates or properties are no longer in ownership or factored by Southside Housing Association, or where Southside Housing Association have been unable to obtain consent to proceed with the service from factored owners.
The Contract term will be for an initial two year period commencing on 1st April 2027 with optional annual  1 year + 1 year + 1 year extensions up to a maximum contract completion date of 31st March 2032.

tender.title: STAR Housing – Cleaning Services (ID610)
tender.description:
Shropshire Towns and Rural Housing (STAR Housing) is seeking to appoint a suitably qualified and experienced supplier to deliver a comprehensive range of cleaning services across its housing portfolio, communal facilities and corporate premises throughout Shropshire.
The Contract will cover planned, routine, responsive and specialist cleaning services, including communal areas, community facilities, office premises, void property cleaning, environmental and deep cleaning, biohazard cleaning, waste removal and needle sweep services, as further detailed in the Procurement Documents.
STAR Housing intends to appoint a single supplier responsible for delivering the full scope of services under one Contract. The Contract will have an initial term of three (3) years, with options to extend for up to two (2) additional years, exercisable as two separate one-year extensions, subject to satisfactory performance and the Contract terms.
The Procurement will be conducted in accordance with the Procurement Act 2023 using the Competitive Flexible Procedure.
The Procurement will comprise the following stages:
Stage 1 – Conditions of Participation: Interested suppliers will be required to complete and submit the Conditions of Participation documentation by the specified deadline. Submissions will be assessed against the published participation requirements and shortlisting methodology. Up to five suppliers may be shortlisted to progress to Stage 2.
Stage 2 – Invitation to Tender: Shortlisted suppliers will be invited to submit detailed proposals, including Quality, Price and Social Value responses. Tenders will be evaluated in accordance with the published award criteria and methodology.
Stage 3 – Optional Interviews: STAR Housing reserves the right to undertake interviews with up to three of the highest-scoring eligible suppliers to clarify and verify information submitted during Stage 2, in accordance with the Procurement Documents.
The Contract will be awarded to the supplier submitting the Most Advantageous Tender, subject to satisfying the applicable procurement requirements.
This notice constitutes the formal commencement of the competitive procurement process. Suppliers wishing to participate must submit their Stage 1 responses through the designated eSourcing portal by the published deadline.
Stage 1: Shropshire Towns and Rural Housing Limited (STAR Housing) is seeking to appoint one suitably qualified and experienced supplier to provide planned, scheduled and responsive cleaning and associated environmental services across its residential properties, communal facilities and corporate premises throughout Shropshire.
The services include ready-to-let void property cleaning; specialist void and environmental deep cleaning; cleaning of communal entrances, staircases and shared residential areas; community rooms and shared facilities; young persons’ accommodation; office cleaning; specialist biohazard cleaning; waste removal and disposal; and needle sweep services.
Services will be delivered across occupied and unoccupied properties and operational buildings. The appointed supplier will provide the personnel, supervision, equipment, cleaning materials, transport and specialist resources required to deliver the full scope safely and consistently, in accordance with the specified standards, frequencies and response requirements.
The requirement will be awarded as a single contract and is not divided into lots. The anticipated commencement date is 2 August 2027. The initial contract term is three years, with options for two further extensions of one year each, giving a maximum duration of five years. The estimated total value over the maximum term is £1,250,000 inclusive of VAT. This estimate does not guarantee expenditure or volumes of work.
The procurement will use the Competitive Flexible Procedure under the Procurement Act 2023, comprising Stage 1 – Conditions of Participation, Stage 2 – Invitation to Tender and an optional Stage 3 – Interview and Tender Verification.
This notice invites requests to participate at Stage 1. Interested suppliers must complete and submit the Procurement Specific Questionnaire through eSourcing Data in accordance with the procurement documents. Only suppliers shortlisted following Stage 1 will be invited to submit a tender at Stage 2.

tender.title: Tender for Residential and Nursing Care Home Partnership Framework in Herefordshire
tender.description:
Herefordshire Council is seeking to establish a multi-provider Care Home Partnerships Framework for the provision of residential care, nursing care and other associated care home services for adults with eligible care and support needs (the 'Services').
This procurement establishes an Open Framework Scheme under section 49 of the Procurement Act 2023.  This Tender Notice relates to the opportunity to apply for admission to the first Herefordshire Care Home Partnerships Framework (the Framework) within the Open Framework Scheme.
The Framework will support the delivery of long-term partnership arrangements between the Council and care home providers. The Services under the Open Framework Scheme and the Framework are 'light touch' as defined by section 9 of the Procurement Act 2023 and are governed by the rules relating to light touch contracts under the Procurement Act 2023.
The Framework will be available to residential and nursing care providers operating eligible care home services and is intended to support approximately 700 to 750 Council-funded placements at any one time across the market, with an anticipated 500 to 550 placements being delivered through formal partnership arrangements. 
The Council has a Partnership and Provider Support Programme which this Open Framework Scheme is part of. The programme is an initiative for all providers commissioned through the Community Wellbeing Directorate of Herefordshire Council and is designed to support genuine collaborative working between Herefordshire Council and providers, promoting high-quality services, improved resident outcomes and a sustainable local care market. Providers admitted to the Framework may participate as a Framework Provider, Partner Provider or Strategic Partner Provider. Eligibility for each level is determined by the applicable Framework requirements, including any required commitment of capacity at the tendered Partnership Rate. Different levels of participation attract different engagement, development and support opportunities.
The Open Framework will have a maximum duration of eight years and an estimated maximum value of approximately £484 million over the full term. The Council does not guarantee that the Open Framework Scheme will continue for the full term of 8 years and no guarantee is given as to the actual value of any framework agreement under the Open Framework Scheme, or any call-off contracts entered under any framework agreement. 
The Open Framework Scheme will be re-opened to new providers at least once in the first three years following the award of the first Framework and at least once during each subsequent five-year period until the expiry of the scheme. Herefordshire Council reserves the right to re-open the Open Framework Scheme at additional intervals where it considers this necessary to support market development, increase provider participation, respond to changes in service demand, address emerging care needs, encourage innovation or maintain sufficient capacity across the sector.
Neither admission to the framework nor any ranking or partnership designation guarantees a minimum number or value of placements. Placements remain subject to assessed need, suitability, resident choice, capacity, the applicable call-off mechanism and the Council's statutory duties.
The Council has considered the use of lots and has structured the procurement into lots reflecting the categories of care required by Herefordshire residents. The service is divided into 2 Lots, under which there are Categories of Care for which providers are required for submit a tender for.  These are:
Lot 1 - Older Persons Residential and Nursing Care
Lot 2 - Working Age Adults
Each Lot contains specific Categories of Care which must be applied for separately. Providers will be evaluated for admission to each lot against the published conditions of participation and award criteria, including quality and price, using the weightings and methodology set out in the tender documents. Individual placements will subsequently be allocated in accordance with the published placement process, taking account of assessed need, suitability, availability, lawful resident choice, Provider Status and Provider Ranked Score.
Across both lots, placements will be subject to assessed need, suitability, availability and lawful resident choice. Eligible care homes will normally be considered in order of Provider Status, then Provider Ranked Score within each level. For Lot 2 (Working Age Adults), matching will reflect specialist support requirements and relevant family and community connections, with searches extended beyond Herefordshire where suitable local provision is unavailable. Any objectively justified departure from the normal placement order will be recorded.
The Council is seeking to award multiple contracts to eligible providers who meet the requirements for each of the Lots. Bidders are referred to the invitation to tender document for full details as it contains specific rules on how bidders may submit their response. Providers may be awarded multiple Lots. Subject to satisfying the conditions of participation and award criteria applicable to the relevant lot and Category of Care (as defined in the invitation to tender), there is no maximum number of providers that may be admitted to a particular Lot under the Framework. 
Bidders are referred to the invitation to tender and procurement documentation for full details.

tender.description:
We are inviting expressions of interest from experienced suppliers for Technology Disconnections and Street Lighting Diversions on the Lower Thames Crossing Roads North programme. The works support the Roads North Temporary Diversions (RNoT), including the A13 and M25 temporary diversion routes.

Package Scope
 The package includes, but is not limited to:
Technology disconnections, diversions and alteration works on the M25.
Street lighting diversions and alterations on the M25, A13, A1089 and associated side roads.
Disconnection, relocation, modification and reconnection of street lighting and technology assets.
Alterations to lighting feeder pillars, electrical supplies, cabling and associated infrastructure.
Alterations and diversions to technology electrical infrastructure (EI).
Installation, relocation or replacement of lighting columns, luminaires, cabling and equipment.
Testing, inspection, commissioning and certification of completed works.
Managing temporary and permanent arrangements to maintain safe operation of affected systems.
Producing test certification, commissioning records and as-built information.
Coordinating with the Contractor, Design Team and stakeholders to meet programme and design requirements.

Suppliers should be able to:
Deliver highway technology disconnections, diversions and street lighting works on operational road networks.
Undertake electrical isolation, installation, testing and commissioning.
Demonstrate experience working safely on live highways, including strategic roads and motorways.
Manage interfaces with existing highway technology and lighting infrastructure.
Provide robust quality assurance and testing processes.
Deliver within challenging programme and traffic management constraints.
Work collaboratively with Tier 1 contractors, designers and stakeholders.

Experience & Standards
 We are looking for companies with:
Proven experience delivering street lighting diversions and highway technology works on major infrastructure projects.
Experience in feeder pillar alterations, circuit modifications, electrical disconnections/reconnections and lighting works.
Appropriately qualified personnel for electrical installation, isolation, inspection, testing and commissioning.
Strong health, safety, environmental and quality management systems.
Experience working within National Highways and/or local authority environments.
Ability to meet Lower Thames Crossing requirements relating to sustainability, carbon reduction and social value.

We actively welcome expressions of interest from SMEs with the relevant experience and capability.

Next Steps
 If you are interested and would like further information, including pre-qualification requirements and tender timelines, please respond by 23.11.26.

Additional information: The Lower Thames Crossing (LTC) is a new road to better connect Essex and Kent through a tunnel beneath the River Thames. Our purpose is to drive a change in how we deliver - connecting people to jobs and businesses to opportunities, leaving a skills legacy for the local community and construction industry, all whilst restoring nature and drawing a new blueprint for low-carbon construction.

Our ambition is to deliver the UK's greenest road, and to do the right thing for local communities and the environment. We can only achieve this with the support of our supply chain, and it is therefore critical that for any supplier to be successful in winning work on LTC, they must demonstrate commitments to supporting delivery of our ambitions:

• Delivering the works through a 'zero emissions' solution, and not using diesel on site in any plant or machinery.

• Supporting us to leave a skills legacy for the local community, by not only recruiting locally, but upskilling your workforce to enable meaningful progression into higher paid higher skilled work.

• Helping to facilitate successful opportunities by providing early careers roles, as well as inspiring young people into construction through delivery of STEM engagement.

tender.description:
This opportunity supports the delivery of the HS2 programme and involves the transportation of precast concrete slab-track units from the PACADAR UK factory to multiple locations along the HS2 route. The requirement is for approximately 12,000 slabs, equating to around 2,400 HGV loads, making it a significant logistics package with a consistent volume of work.
      
      Suppliers will be required to provide suitable HGV transport capable of safely carrying five slab units per load while complying with all relevant transport, safety and load restraint regulations. Deliveries will be made to various locations along the HS2 corridor, with loading at the factory and offloading at site undertaken by others.
      
      Interested suppliers will be asked to demonstrate their transport capability, available fleet capacity and proposed delivery approach, together with competitive commercial rates. Further information on the scope, delivery requirements, indicative volumes and pricing structure is available within the attached documentation.
